item.title: Passive Retirement Investing Raises Systemic Risk for US Markets
item.description: Like it or not, we are all betting on AI taking over the economy. In the last 40 years, the US has become a nation of stock investors. On the whole, it has made Americans rich. Now the stock market is soaring on the hopes that AI will make everyone more productive — and if that doesn’t work out, we all may learn the definition of a bad tail risk.
item.dc:creator: Allison Schrager

item.title: A Texas Magnet Plant Shows US Manufacturing Can Return — at a Cost
item.description: On former farmland on the outskirts of Fort Worth, Texas, a brand-new 250,000-square-foot factory stands as a symbol that the US can return to its roots of making things.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Black

item.title: Can Democrats' Blue-Collar Brigade Win Working-Class Voters?
item.description: Sam Forstag recently joined a text chain to better keep up with a few friends. There’s nothing unusual about that, except Forstag’s texting buddies are a group of Democratic candidates for the US House who share one unusual characteristic: They have spent years in blue-collar jobs.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Brownstein

item.title: Midterms: Democrats Are Set to Win the House but Not in a Blue Wave
item.description: The Republican majority in the House of Representatives is almost certainly headed for a massive whupping in the upcoming midterm elections. But the tussle for the speaker’s gavel is not unfolding, and may not finish, like the thumpings and shellackings of yesteryear.
item.dc:creator: David M. Drucker

item.title: Pete Hegseth's Pentagon Purges Must Be Stopped by Congress
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his critics agree on one thing: The Pentagon is in urgent need of transformation. The change he’s pursuing, however, is endangering that vital mission.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Crypto Can't Go Mainstream Without the Clarity Act
item.description: US regulators are determined to boost cryptoassets. That’s unsurprising when they owe their jobs to the meme-coin billionaire (and US President) Donald Trump. But after the Senate last week voted down the wide-ranging Clarity Act, any efforts by market watchdogs to codify rules for digital-asset markets risk being shot down by the next administration. And worse, the Supreme Court has already undercut agency rulemaking powers, anyway.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Trump-Xi Summit: China’s Leverage Makes It Key to Any Iran War Deal
item.description: At the BRICS summit in New Delhi on Sept. 12, 2026, Xi Jinping called for a more active role for China and other member countries in ending the war with Iran. China’s president said the conflict had inflicted serious losses across the region, was against the common interests of the international community, and should give way to a “permanent, comprehensive ceasefire” and a new regional security architecture. item.title: Germany Is Stuck With Merz When It Needs a Klopp
item.description: Two more humiliating regional election results in eastern Germany have dealt conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s authority a heavy blow. Rather than fall on his sword, Germany’s unpopular leader is urging patience while reforms continue.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bryant

item.title: Oil Market: The $1 Million-a-Day Oil Tanker Will Drive Inflation
item.description: Former President Bill Clinton once said that when a crisis breaks out, the first thing everyone in Washington asks is, “Where is the nearest [aircraft] carrier?” That remains a critical question as the US faces off against Iran in the Strait of Hormuz, but for the shipping industry, it may have been replaced by another: “Where are the nearest oil tankers — and do we have enough?”
item.dc:creator: Javier Blas

item.title: Burnham’s Good Vibes Aren’t Enough for Bond Markets
item.description: British voters, like American ones, usually prefer the candidate most comfortable in their skin — if not always the best qualified for the job.
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivens

item.title: AIndicators: Fed Hiking Cycle Is a Red-Flag Moment
item.description: The question is whether credit markets will keep signalling calm.
item.dc:creator: John Authers and Richard Abbey

item.title: LVMH Shares Are Cheap — for a Reason
item.description: Earlier this year, LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE opened a Louis Vuitton Hotel in London, a pop-up celebrating 130 years of the brand’s distinctive monogram. Investors, though, have been checking out of the world’s biggest luxury goods group.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Felsted

item.title: The Policy Muddle Snaring the World’s Big Central Banks
item.description: Policymakers in the UK, US and Japan are trying to pull off a high-wire act: They’re leaning against rising longer-term government bond yields even as they talk tough on inflation. It amounts to hitting the accelerator and brakes at the same time. Conspicuously absent from the discussions are any serious attempts at taking the politically difficult decisions needed to rein in unsustainable national debts and create a healthier policy mix for the economy. item.title: It’s Tough Being a Small Economy Like the Philippines in an AI Boom
item.description: You have to feel sorry for the Philippines. An economy that was doing very nicely has once again become Southeast Asia’s straggler, even though officials are doing many right things. Painful as it is, they should stick to their guns.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss
